newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile supermarket chain D&S issues bonds.
newsitem.headline: Chile supermarket chain D&S issues bonds.

text.p: Chilean supermarket chain D&S will issue local bonds worth $120 million in two equal tranches this year, said general manager Nicolas Ibanez.
The first will be in the April-June quarter and the second towards the end of the year, Ibanez told reporters at the company's shareholder meeting.
The funds from the issue will be used to finance the investment plans of the group which owns the Ekono, Almac and Lider supermarket chains, he said.
The company is also planning to start trading in New York through the issue of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) at the end of the year or in early 1998, he added.
D&S officials have said the firm will invest $500 million in the next four years in expanding its business in Chile and Argentina.
Ibanez said the company expects to report net profits this year of $52 million, up 24 percent from 1996, he said.
One Chilean supermarket chain, Santa Isabel already trades in New York, while another, Unimarc, is in the process of placing ADRs.
